from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import yaml

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
REQS_FILE = REPO_ROOT / "backend" / "requirements-tooling.txt"
PRECOMMIT_FILE = REPO_ROOT / ".pre-commit-config.yaml"

# Maps a requirements-tooling.txt package name to the pre-commit repo URL whose
# `rev:` must match it. Only tools that exist in BOTH files are guarded here —
# bandit/pre-commit itself have no pre-commit-hook counterpart.
_TRACKED_REPOS = {
    "ruff": "astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit",
    "black": "psf/black",
    "mypy": "pre-commit/mirrors-mypy",
}


def _parse_requirements_pins(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return {package: version} for the packages this guard tracks."""
    pins: dict[str, str] = {}
    for raw in path.read_text().splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#"):
            continue
        match = re.match(r"^([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)(?:\[[^\]]*\])?==([^\s]+)$", line)
        if match and match.group(1).lower() in _TRACKED_REPOS:
            pins[match.group(1).lower()] = match.group(2)
    return pins


def _parse_precommit_revs(path: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return {repo_url_suffix: rev} for every repo block in the config.

    Parsed as YAML rather than matched with a regex against `repo:`/`rev:` line
    adjacency — a comment or blank line between the two (e.g. explaining why a
    version is pinned) is valid YAML but would silently break a positional regex
    match, reporting a false "repo not found" drift error.
    """
    doc = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text())
    revs: dict[str, str] = {}
    for repo in doc.get("repos", []):
        url = repo.get("repo", "")
        rev = repo.get("rev")
        if url.startswith("https://github.com/") and rev is not None:
            revs[url.removeprefix("https://github.com/")] = str(rev)
    return revs

content.text:
## The `ids` unbound warning

Pyright flagged this in `test_incident_service.py`'s two race tests (`test_concurrent_failing_syncs_no_duplicate` and `test_concurrent_manual_resolves_exactly_one_wins`). Shape:

```python
def test_concurrent_failing_syncs_no_duplicate(_db_engine):
    seed = SASession(bind=_db_engine)
    try:
        ...
        ids = {...}          # assigned partway through the try block
        ...
    finally:
        seed.close()
        _cleanup(_db_engine, **ids)   # <-- reads `ids` unconditionally
```

`ids` is only assigned partway through the `try` block (after `_user`/`_connection`/`_suite`/`_check`/`_run_with_result` have all succeeded). If any of those seeding calls raises before `ids = {...}` runs, control jumps straight to `finally`, and `_cleanup(_db_engine, **ids)` then raises `NameError: name 'ids' is not defined` — which **masks the original exception** with a confusing, unrelated secondary error. Pyright's `reportPossiblyUnboundVariable` is catching a real path, not just being pedantic.

It's pre-existing (predates this session — confirmed against `git log`) and unrelated to the timeout work I just did in that file, so per this repo's own rule ("every finding ends fixed or filed, never dropped"), I'll file it as an issue rather than scope-creep it into the just-merged PR.

cd /Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ
gh issue create --title "test_incident_service.py: NameError masks the real failure if seeding raises before \`ids\` is assigned" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What

Both concurrency-race tests in `backend/tests/services/test_incident_service.py` (`test_concurrent_failing_syncs_no_duplicate`, `test_concurrent_manual_resolves_exactly_one_wins`) follow this shape:

```python
def test_concurrent_failing_syncs_no_duplicate(_db_engine: Any) -> None:
    seed = SASession(bind=_db_engine)
    try:
        owner = _user(seed, ...)
        conn = _connection(seed, owner)
        suite = _suite(seed, owner, conn, ...)
        check = _check(seed, suite)
        ...
        ids = {"suite_id": suite.id, "asset_id": suite.asset_id, "conn_id": conn.id, "user_id": owner.id}
        ...
    finally:
        seed.close()
        _cleanup(_db_engine, **ids)   # reads `ids` unconditionally
```

`ids` is only assigned after `_user`/`_connection`/`_suite`/`_check` have all succeeded. Pyright flags it `reportPossiblyUnboundVariable` because if any of those seeding calls raises, control jumps to `finally` before `ids` exists.

## Why it matters

`_cleanup(_db_engine, **ids)` in that case raises `NameError: name 'ids' is not defined`, which replaces/masks whatever the original seeding failure was (e.g. a real DB constraint violation) with an unrelated, confusing secondary error — the actual root cause never surfaces in the test output.

## Fix

Initialize `ids: dict[str, Any] | None = None` before the `try`, assign it normally inside, and guard the cleanup: `if ids is not None: _cleanup(_db_engine, **ids)`. Applies to both race tests in the file.

## Found by

Pyright, surfaced while adding `_BARRIER_TIMEOUT`/`_JOIN_TIMEOUT` to the same tests (#1411, PR #1496) — pre-existing, not introduced by that change.
EOF
)" --label bug,test

`backend/tests/api/test_assets.py` opens with:

> The ADR-0033 **Viewer** role is N/A here: it is not built yet (#740-#743 open), so the ladder under test is owner / edit / view / no-share / workspace-admin. When Viewer lands (#741) it caps at `view`, so it will fold into the view-share rows.

**#740, #741, #742 and #743 are all CLOSED** — the RBAC track shipped 2026-08-16. The stated reason for the gap no longer holds.

## Why this is more than a stale comment

The `viewer` identifiers throughout that file are per-suite **`view` shares** (ADR 0027), not the workspace **`viewer` role** (ADR 0033). They are different axes, and the file's own header says so. So the assertion is still *accurate* — the workspace Viewer role genuinely is not exercised against `/assets` — while its justification is now false.

git add backend/tests/services/test_incident_service.py
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
fix: don't let an early seeding failure mask itself with UnboundLocalError

Both concurrency-race tests in test_incident_service.py assign `ids`
partway through their try block, then read it unconditionally in
finally to clean up committed rows. If any seeding call before that
assignment raises, `finally`'s `_cleanup(**ids)` masks the real failure
with `UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'ids'...` instead
— the original root cause never reaches the test output. Reproduced the
exact shape standalone to confirm.

Declares `ids: dict[str, uuid.UUID] | None = None` before the try and
guards the cleanup call, so a seeding failure surfaces as itself.

Fixes #1498
EOF
)"
git push -u origin fix/issue-1498-ids-unbound-in-incident-race-tests
